Covariance Matrices and Cholesky Factors of the Fitted Models

Source: R/covariance_table.R
covariance_table.Rd

Reports, for each fitted model, the covariance matrix of the parameter estimates or its Cholesky factor, on the transformed (real-line) scale on which flexsurv estimates the parameters and/or on the natural scale.

Usage

covariance_table(
  x,
  type = c("covariance", "cholesky"),
  scale = c("transformed", "natural")
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

type

"covariance" (the default) or "cholesky".

scale

Character vector with "transformed" and/or "natural". The default is both.

Value

A data frame with the columns fit_type, arm, model, scale, row, col (parameter names) and value, with one row per element of the matrix of each fitted model, row by row (the elements above the diagonal of the Cholesky factor are 0). Values are NA when the covariance matrix is not available or not positive definite.

Details

The covariance matrix on the transformed scale is the inverse of the Hessian of minus the log-likelihood computed by flexsurv. On the natural scale it is J V J (delta method), with J the diagonal matrix of the derivatives of the natural parameters with respect to the transformed ones (the estimate itself for a log-transformed parameter, 1 otherwise). The Cholesky factor is the lower triangular matrix L with L %*% t(L) equal to the covariance matrix; correlated normal draws for probabilistic sensitivity analysis are est + L z with z independent standard normal. Draws should be made on the transformed scale, where the asymptotic normal distribution is used by flexsurv and positive parameters stay positive after back-transformation. The parameters are those of parameter_table.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = "weibull",
                            spline_scales = NULL)
covariance_table(fits)
